subject: AWS Marketplace entitlement matrix + short page snippet suggestions
messages:
From: Pedro Martinez <pedro@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@aws-partnernet.amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial entitlement questions and short copy ask

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. AWS partner ops asked us to clarify the entitlements and user tiers on the listing — they need a simple matrix they can surface to the procurement team. Quick asks:

- Can you send a single-sheet entitlement matrix that maps SKU / tier -> included features (enclave, dedup cache, monthly usage quota)?
- We also need a few short copy snippets (20-40 words) that clearly state differences between Developer / Business / Enterprise plans for the product page. AWS wants concise bullets for the hero and for the pricing table.

I attached our internal pricing language but it’s not formatted for Marketplace. If you or Ben can draft the matrix + snippets we’ll validate and push to AWS.

Appreciate the help — Pedro

Attachments: acme-current-pricing.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Pedro Martinez <pedro@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@aws-partnernet.amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial entitlement questions and short copy ask

Pedro —

Thanks, attaching an initial pass. I converted your current tiers into a compact entitlement matrix and provided three short snippets for hero/pricing table. Highlights:

- Matrix: maps SKUs to feature toggles (KV cache, private VPC option, burst capacity) + per-seat vs. per-token billing column.
- Snippets: three variants for hero (developer, business, enterprise) and two alternate lines for the pricing table.
- Note: I flagged one entitlement that needs legal confirmation (data residency language under Enterprise).

Ben/Vanessa — please review the attached XLSX (tab: "Marketplace matrix v2") and the snippet doc. Ben — can you check the billing phrasing to ensure it aligns with our on-invoice wording? Vanessa — any marketplace copy suggestions for the hero tone?

Next milestone: finalize before AWS review on Wed 15th.

Best,
Evelyn
Director, GTM Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: entitlement-matrix-v2.xlsx; offer-snippets-v3.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Pedro Martinez <pedro@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial entitlement questions and short copy ask

Thanks for the draft, Evelyn. Quick notes after a pass:

- Billing phrasing: change "per-token credits" to "consumption credits" for marketplace listing to avoid confusion with our internal metering language.
- SKUs: recommend adding an explicit SKU for "Dedicated (Reserved)" to map to Enterprise entitlements. AWS procurement asked for that mapping.
- Add a short one-line callout for the private deployment option under Enterprise (compliance-focused buyers like to see this up front).

I made inline comments in entitlement-matrix-v2.xlsx and added an extra row in the snippets doc with a more concise hero line.

Ben

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial entitlement questions and short copy ask

All — I like the tighter hero lines. A couple of editorial suggestions for marketplace readability:

- Hero: prefer an active-benefit approach — e.g., "Run LLM workloads with predictable latency and pay-for-what-you-use" vs. feature-first phrasing.
- Pricing table bullets: use consistent units (either tokens/minutes or seats) — mixing units confuses listing reviewers. Suggest tokens for Developer and Business, seats+support for Enterprise.
- Short FAQ snippet: add a one-line "what's included" for each tier to reduce support tickets after launch.

Aisha — can you confirm whether AWS has a preferred term for reserved capacity SKU naming? Pedro — I updated the snippets doc and screenshot (usage-plan) to reflect these edits.

- Vanessa

On Mon, Sep 13, 2027 at 3:27 PM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@aws-partnernet.amazon.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Pedro Martinez <pedro@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial entitlement questions and short copy ask

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A couple of AWS-side clarifications before we finalize the Marketplace draft:

1) SKU naming: AWS prefers a clear pattern: <Product>-<OfferingType>-<Term> (example: RedwoodInference-Enterprise-Annual). A short note in the matrix mapping will help procurement.
2) Entitlements: the matrix looks good but please ensure the data residency/responsibility language is explicit for Enterprise (e.g., "Customer controls data residency; vendor processes at customer-controlled endpoints").
3) Snippets: the hero lines are fine — keep one concise alternative that can be used for the AWS marketplace hero and one slightly longer line for the product description.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk AWS listing ops through the final matrix if you can have the updated files pushed to the shared link by EOD.

Aisha Khan
AWS Partner Programs
